'''Praveen Chaudhari''' (November 30, 1937 – January 12, 2010)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tributes.com/show/Praveen-Chaudhari-87661096 |title=Praveen Chaudhari 1937 - 2010 - Obituary |publisher=Tributes.com |date= |accessdate=August 12, 2010}}</ref> was an [[Indian American]] physicist who has contributed to the field of [[material physics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ctns.org/ssq/csit_bios.html |title=CTNS-Science and the Spiritual Quest |publisher=Ctns.org |date=September 1, 2001 |accessdate=August 12, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1016/S1359-0286(99)80003-5| title = Electronic materials| journal = Current Opinion in Solid State and Materials Science| volume = 4| issue = 1| pages = 3| year = 1999| last1 = Tarascon | first1 = J. M. | last2 = Chaudhari | first2 = P. | bibcode = 1999COSSM...4....3T}}</ref> His research focused on structure and properties of amorphous solids, defects in solids, mechanical properties of thin films, superconductivity, quantum transport in disordered systems, liquid crystal alignment on substrates, and the magnetic monopole experiment.<ref name="Obituary">{{cite web|url=http://www.northshoreoflongisland.com/Obituary-10456.112114_Praveen_Chaudhari.html |title=Praveen Chaudhari Obituary |website=Northshoreoflongisland.com |date= |accessdate=August 12, 2010}}</ref>  He published numerous papers and filed 22 patents, most notably one for the erasable read-write compact discs which are commonly used to burn music.<ref>{{cite web|last=Dreifus |first=Claudia |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2003/10/21/science/conversation-with-praveen-chaudhari-new-chief-physics-lab-tries-polish-faded.html |title=A CONVERSATION WITH - PRAVEEN CHAUDHARI - New Chief at Physics Lab Tries to Polish Faded Star - Interview |website=New York Times.|date=October 21, 2003 |publisher=Vanderbilt University}}</ref>

He was at IBM for 36 years during which he was appointed director and later vice president of science in 1981 and 1982.  In 2004, he became director of [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] (BNL) and stepped down in 2006.

Praveen died on January 12, 2010, at the age of 72.<ref name="Obituary" />

==Accomplishments==
Chaudhari was a member of scientific institutions such as the [[National Academy of Engineering]], the National Academy of Sciences, the American Academy of Arts and Sciences and the [[American Physical Society]]. He served as executive secretary of President Reagan's Advisory Council on Superconductivity and served on the US National Critical Technology Panel.<ref name="autogenerated1">{{cite web|url=http://www.bnl.gov/today/story.asp?ITEM_NO=1598 |title=In Memoriam: Praveen Chaudhari |publisher=Bnl.gov |date= |accessdate=August 12, 2010}}</ref>

His awards include the National Medal for Technology,<ref name="columbia1">{{cite web|url=http://engineering.columbia.edu/web/newsletter/spring_2010/memoriam |title=Engineering Newsletter |publisher=Engineering.columbia.edu |date= |accessdate=August 12, 2010}}</ref> the American Physical Society's George E. Pake Award, the Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Inc., Morris N. Liebmann Memorial Award, the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] Harry C. Gatos Distinguished Lecture and Prize, and the National Medal of Technology.<ref name="iim-india1">{{cite web |url=http://www.iim-india.net/page.php?id=212 |title=In Memoriam: Praveen Chaudhari |publisher=Indian Institute of Metal |accessdate=August 12, 2010 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20121018012610/http://iim-india.net/page.php?id=212 |archivedate=October 18, 2012 }}</ref>
